description:
v1.0 | 213 gates | 4 ticks
https://github.com/byggmesterPRO/pareto-circuits

16 words of 4 bits. The word at the address is always on the outputs.

A RAM stores many numbers at once, each in its own numbered slot. Use it for a lookup table, a list of stored settings, or the working memory of a small computer.

Set the address inputs to the slot you want, and its number is always shown on the outputs. To store a number, set the data inputs to it and pulse the write input for exactly one tick. The address and data must stay steady until after the pulse. A button or switch is too slow, so send it through a one-tick pulse maker first. All slots start at zero.

Inputs (yellow gates, first row, lowest bit first): address = x 0-3, data = x 4-7, write = x 8 (a pulse of exactly one tick).
Outputs (green gates): the word at the address = x 0-3.

Profile: fast, the build with the fewest ticks for this size.
How it works: Each bit is an XOR gate wired to itself; every cell reads the address itself.
Ticks from an input to the outputs: 4. From a pulse to the outputs: 5. Inputs steady before a pulse: 5.
Checked with thousands of random operations in a simulator. Gates include the input gates; ticks count the input gate too.
By: byggmesterPRO
